title: How to Build a Customer Journey Map for Your Small Business

facts.fact: The page states that a customer journey is broadly divided into three stages: before purchase, purchase and usage, and after purchase.
facts.quote: Broadly, there are three stages of the customer journey to consider: before purchase, purchase and usage, and after purchase.

facts.fact: The page defines a customer journey map as a visual representation of the ways a customer interacts with a brand before and after they make a purchase.
facts.quote: A customer journey map is a visual representation of the ways a customer interacts with your brand before and after they make a purchase.

facts.fact: The page says a customer journey is similar to a sales funnel.
facts.quote: A customer journey is similar to a sales funnel.

facts.fact: The page says most customer journey maps start with the awareness phase, which is when someone discovers the company.
facts.quote: Most customer journey maps start with the**awareness** phase.

facts.fact: The page repeats a marketing adage that 80% of a business's revenue comes from 20% of its customers; the page presents this as a famous adage and does not cite a source or study for it.
facts.quote: The famous marketing adage that 80% of your business comes from 20% of your customers

facts.fact: The page lists solicited data sources as surveys, focus groups, and online reviews.
facts.quote: Surveys, focus groups, and online reviews can help you form a picture of how your customers experience your business.

facts.fact: The page names Forrester and Mintel as market research sources that can help small businesses understand target customers.
facts.quote: Market research from sites like Forrester and Mintel can also help you understand your target customer on a deeper level.

facts.fact: The page names UXPressia and Smaply as dedicated tools for creating complex customer journey maps, and Miro and Mural as template sites that offer free or paid templates.
facts.quote: There are dedicated tools that can create complex customer journey maps, such as UXPressia or Smaply.

facts.fact: The page promotes a free AI training course for small businesses that teaches the basics of AI in about 30 minutes.
facts.quote: Learn the basics of AI in just 30 minutes

facts.fact: The page was published on January 8, 2026 at 8:16 PM Eastern time according to its metadata, while the page text also shows a 'Published February 02, 2026' date.
